preview: This episode looks at personalized news feeds and how they shape a reader’s path through the news. They can make relevant stories easier to find, but they also raise questions about what may be left out and how much of the process a reader can see or control. As you listen, consider this: who is shaping what a reader understands, and how much choice does the reader really have?
comment_1: Listen for how the two readers feel about the way their news is chosen for them.
comment_2: Now, we’ll hear different voices, one after another, sharing how they see this kind of news feed.
comment_3: You have now heard two different ways of experiencing the same kind of feed. Instead of deciding which voice is right, let’s look at why the same situation can feel so different to different people.
comment_4: So the question is not only which reader is right. It is also what makes this situation feel so different to each person, and what is happening underneath what they can see.
